public_rationale: Research within the period demonstrates unexpected failures and clear human–model behavioral differences. That supports the ordinary, limited reading of 'unpredictable' and 'not always human like.' Other experiments show that humans can sometimes anticipate machine errors, so a claim of complete unpredictability would go beyond the evidence.
limitations: The result depends on reading unpredictable as surprising failures rather than universal unpredictability.
These studies do not establish a universal difference between human cognition and every deep-learning architecture.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The past seven years of AI have shown that deep learning is unpredictable and not always human-like.

statement.excerpt: Seven years of AI has taught us that deep learning is unpredictable, and not always human like.

our_interpretation: The surrounding reference to March 2016 anchors the approximately seven-year period.
The ordinary reading is that successful deep-learning systems have exhibited surprising failures and sometimes behaved differently from humans on comparable tasks.
Unpredictable is read as unexpected failure under changed inputs, not mathematical randomness or an inability to predict any output.
criteria.support_condition: Research during the stated period documents surprising failures and observable differences between deep-learning systems and humans.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The relevant comparisons show that the alleged failures were not reproducible or that the purported behavioral differences disappear under appropriate controls.

evidence.excerpt: CNN recognition accuracies were much lower than human accuracies.
evidence.locator: Section 3.1, Texture vs shape bias in humans and ImageNet-trained CNNs
evidence.publisher: Geirhos et al., ICLR paper hosted on arXiv
evidence.explanation: Humans and networks classified the same images differently. The experiments also identified differing reliance on shape and texture.

evidence.excerpt: classifies as an espresso at every angle!
evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning 'Our process works for arbitrary 3D models'
evidence.explanation: The authors demonstrated a physical object that produced a conspicuously unexpected classification across viewpoints. This supports the ordinary claim about surprising failures.

evidence.excerpt: Human intuition may be a surprisingly reliable guide to machine (mis)classification
evidence.explanation: Across adversarial-image experiments, people could often anticipate machine labels. This limits any stronger claim that deep-learning behavior is wholly unintelligible or never human-like.
